metadata.scope: New Zealand national institutions and implemented policy under the incumbent coalition, including relevant local variation. Electoral competition and implementation are assessed separately from constitutional design. Campaign promises and measures not yet in force are not treated as implemented policy. All fifteen axes have research briefs, but this unfinished draft retains eighteen specific unresolved questions. Causal-trait answers draw on retained official guidance and operational frameworks, with scope limitations recorded individually. Completion on 2026-10-05 resolves eighteen earlier gaps with provisional educated assumptions, not documented adopted positions. Earlier unresolved text remains as historical review context.

axes.brief: Parliamentary confidence, competitive elections and independent legal review constrain government. Assessment includes the incumbent coalition and 2026 electoral rules, not just constitutional design.
axes.counterEvidence: The monarchy is unelected; courts cannot invalidate Acts of Parliament. Citizen-initiated referendums are advisory and there is no enforceable voter recall. The 2026 electoral rules restrict prisoner voting and end election-day enrolment. September 2026 parliamentary scrutiny exposed incomplete official evidence about a terminated biometric project: accountability mechanisms exist, but disclosure can fail. Sources: constitution; high-court-role; referendums; electing-mps; election-2026-kit; scrutiny-biometric-2026.

axes.brief: Civil-liberty protections coexist with drug prohibitions, judicially authorised surveillance, risk-based control orders and gang dispersal powers. Current implementation includes the 2025 drug-driving regime, 2026 ANPR use and a 2026 independent finding upholding urgent warrantless home entry.
axes.counterEvidence: The IPCA found unlawful interference with peaceful protesters and uncertain obstruction powers; that is evidence about practice, not proof that its proposed reforms became law. Routine ANPR retention differs from permanent investigation files. A warrantless home search can be lawful to prevent escape or loss of evidence without an immediate safety emergency. The September 2026 move-on Act commences a month after 25 September and is excluded from implemented policy at this cut-off; the August Online Safety Bill also remains a proposal. Sources: protest-review-2025; anpr-policy-2026; home-entry-2026; move-on-act-not-commenced; online-safety-bill.
